pages.name: Two squares
pages.task: A shape covers 2 squares. What is its area after `[3 0; 0 2]`?
pages.why: The stretch turns every square into a 3 by 2 box of area 6. The shape has 2 squares, so it covers `2 × 6 = 12`.

pages.name: A shear
pages.text: The shear `[1 1; 0 1]` leans the square over into a parallelogram. Cut the triangle off one end and slide it to the other, and it makes a 1 by 1 square again. So its area is base times height, with the height at right angles to the base.

pages.name: Box it in
pages.text: Box the parallelogram of `[3 1; 1 2]` in a 4 by 3 rectangle, of area 12. The corners take away 3, 2 and 2, which leaves 5. For any `[a b; c d]` the box is `(a + b)(c + d)`, which is `ac + ad + bc + bd`. The corners take away ac, bd and 2bc, which leaves ad − bc. That number is the [[determinant]], written det A or |A| for a matrix A.

pages.name: What −3 means
pages.task: The determinant of `[1 2; 2 1]` is `1 × 1 − 2 × 2 = −3`. What does that say about the move?
pages.answer: It triples every area and flips the plane
pages.why: The size of −3 is 3, so every area triples. The minus sign means the plane flips over, so the flag reads backwards.
